**Action:** step_observation  
**Content:**  
The pump P-101A tripped due to high vibration (7.8 mm/s RMS, over 7.0 mm/s limit) and elevated bearing temperature (92.1°C, over 85°C limit). The discharge pressure (492.5 PSI) exceeded the safe operating range (80-120 PSI). Cavitation symptoms such as rumble, rubbing, or excessive vibration should be checked. The bearing temperature exceeding its limit could indicate a failing component, requiring further inspection.

rca_result_structured.primary_cause_text: The centrifugal compressor K-101 tripped due to exceeding its safety limits for high journal bearing temperature (95.0 °C) and discharge overpressure (450.0 PSI). The system automatically tripped as per the predefined safety protocols. The immediate response included de-energizing the drive motor, opening the emergency relief valve, and initiating a bypass to dissipate momentum. The trip was confirmed by both the thermal and pressure sensors, and no additional evidence is needed to support this conclusion as the system responses are well-documented in the operating procedures.

VENTION PROTOCOL & FOUR-EYES SUPERVISORY GATE

5.1 Immediate Automated Response to Overpressure Surge:
If discharge pressure exceeds 450.0 PSI (31.02 bar) or bearing temperature breaches 95.0 °C:
1. The automated safety interlock trips breaker VCB-101A, de-energizing the main 450 kW drive motor.
2. Emergency Safety Relief Valve SV-402 opens fully, venting trapped hydrocarbon volume into the Flare-Header.
3. Minimum recirculation bypass valve opens 100% to dissipate residual hydraulic momentum.

RCA INCIDENT LOG: HYDROCRACKER R-301 HIGH PRESSURE TRIP
Doc ID: RCA-INC-2026-CHRONO | Unit: 300 | Page 1 of 2


INCIDENT SEQUENCE OF EVENTS:

| Page 1 of 2


INCIDENT SEQUENCE OF EVENTS:

04:10:00 - Unit operating at 100% rated throughput. Reactor pressure normal at 142 bar.
04:12:15 - Feed flow transmitter FT-302 indicated an abrupt drop to 0 m3/h.
04:12:30 - DCS feed flow controller initiated full 100% open demand to control valve FV-302.
04:13:00 - Field operator reported severe banging in preheat loop. Reactor pressure surged to 168 bar.
04:13:45 - High pressure trip interlock PSHH-301 initiated automated emergency depressuring.

EQUIPMENT OVERHAUL LOG: Control Valve FV-302 Turnaround Service
Record: MR-VALVE-FV302 | Equipment Tag: FV-302 | Page 1 of 4


1.0 AS-FOUND INSPECTION SUMMARY
Unit FV-302 was isolated and cleared for complete turnaround disassembly.
Visual inspection of active thrust pads revealed minor babbitt wiping on lower shoes.
Coupling hub inspection showed severe fretting on drive-end taper.

FV-302 (Controller Out)     100.0% (Demand)          HIGH SATURATION

  04:12:45             ZT-302 (Stem Position)     4.2% (Actual)              DEVIATION ERROR

  04:13:00             PT-301 (Reactor Press)      168.4 bar                 HIGH-HIGH TRIP

09:30:12 - Boiler feed pump BFP-02 tripped on main electrical breaker open signal.

Doc ID: RCA-INC-2026-BFP02 | Status: INCONCLUSIVE INVESTIGATION | Page 1 of 2

.

AVAILABLE DATA & MISSING TELEMETRY:
Motor protection relay showed no ground fault or overcurrent trip flags.
SCADA vibration trend recording channel for BFP-02 was offline for calibration.
No acoustic or physical distress observed prior to trip.

SUBSTATION 13.8kV RELAY TRIP EVALUATION
Doc ID: ELEC-LOG-2026-SUB3 | Page 2 of 2


CONCLUSION & INVESTIGATION STATUS:

Transient magnitude was within normal IEEE 1159 voltage sag limits.
Available evidence is insufficient to determine whether trip was electrical or mechanical.
Root cause remains UNCONFIRMED pending sensor telemetry retrieval.
